OVHcloud wants to contribute to Infisical under a **Corporate CLA**. Our first PR, #7523 (OVHcloud KMS token connection), has been blocked by the `cla/signed` check since 2026-08-04 because our engineers may only contribute under a company-level agreement, not the Individual CLA.

items.body: ### Product Platform/Access controls/Other ### Describe the bug When running the self-hosted Infisical Docker image, configuring `CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` at runtime does not configure the hCaptcha site key used by the frontend. The Infisical container correctly receives the configured environment variable. For example: CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY= However, the frontend continues to initialise hCaptcha using the literal placeholder value: captcha-site-key This causes hCaptcha to display: > ERROR for site owner: Invalid site key Inspecting the network request from the browser confirms that the placeholder is being sent to hCaptcha: https://api.hcaptcha.com/checksiteconfig?...&host=&sitekey=captcha-site-key&... Inspecting the running container confirms that the placeholder is embedded inside the compiled frontend JavaScript bundle: /backend/frontend-build/assets/index-v0-165-6-BXoyH3V2.js:captcha-site-key At the same time, inspecting the container environment confirms that the real site key is correctly configured: CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY= It therefore appears that the frontend's hCaptcha site key is being injected at Docker image build time rather than being configurable at container runtime. This prevents features requiring hCaptcha, such as password recovery, from working correctly with the standard self-hosted Docker image even when `CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` and `CAPTCHA_SECRET` are correctly supplied to the container. ### To Reproduce 1. Deploy the official self-hosted Infisical Docker image. 2. Configure valid hCaptcha credentials as environment variables on the Infisical container: CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY= CAPTCHA_SECRET= 3. Confirm that the site key is present inside the running container: docker inspect infisical \ --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' \ | grep -Ei 'CAPTCHA|HCAPTCHA' This correctly returns: CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY= 4. Navigate to a feature which uses hCaptcha, such as the password recovery page. 5. The hCaptcha widget displays: ERROR for site owner: Invalid site key 6. Inspect the hCaptcha `checksiteconfig` request in the browser's developer tools. Despite the container having a valid `CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, the request contains: sitekey=captcha-site-key 7. Search the compiled frontend assets inside the running container: docker exec infisical sh -c \ 'grep -R -l "captcha-site-key" /backend/frontend-build 2>/dev/null | head' On v0.165.6 this returns: /backend/frontend-build/assets/index-v0-165-6-BXoyH3V2.js 8. Confirm the placeholder is embedded in the bundle: docker exec infisical sh -c \ 'grep -R -o "captcha-site-key" /backend/frontend-build 2>/dev/null | head' This returns: /backend/frontend-build/assets/index-v0-165-6-BXoyH3V2.js:captcha-site-key The frontend therefore appears to be using a site key compiled into the Docker image rather than the `CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` supplied to the running container. ### Expected behavior When `CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` is supplied to the self-hosted Infisical container, the frontend should use that value when initialising hCaptcha. For example, given: CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY= the hCaptcha `checksiteconfig` request should contain: sitekey= rather than: sitekey=captcha-site-key A self-hosted deployment should be able to configure both the hCaptcha site key and secret through runtime configuration/environment variables without requiring a custom build of the Infisical Docker image or modification of the compiled frontend assets. If `CAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` is intentionally a build-time-only setting, this should at minimum be clearly documented for self-hosted deployments. However, runtime configuration would be preferable because users of the official pre-built Docker image cannot otherwise provide their own hCaptcha site key. ### Screenshots ### Deployment Type Self-hosted ### Additional context Infisical version: v0.165.6 Docker image: infisical/infisical:v0.165.6 Deployment type: Self-hosted using the official Infisical Docker image. Host OS: Linux (Ubuntu server)

### Product

Platform/Access controls/Other

### Describe the bug

 Project slugs containing underscores (_) can be written but cannot be read back by slug. The update path accepts _; the read-by-slug path rejects it. A project you can rename to <text>_<text>returns a 400 when you try to GET it by that slug.

  Expected behavior

  The set of characters allowed in a project slug is the same whether you're writing it (create/update) or reading it back by slug. If _ is legal when saving, GET /v1/projects/slug/<that slug> should resolve the project.

  Actual behavior

  GET /api/v1/projects/slug/<text>_<text>returns 400:
  Slug field can only contain lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens
  even though the project exists and the slug is valid per the update path.

  Root cause

  Two different validators disagree about what a slug may contain.

  - Write (allowed): PATCH /v1/projects/:projectId, slug field at project-router.ts:507 uses re2Validator(/^[a-z0-9]+(?:[_-][a-z0-9]+)*$/). The [_-] in the pattern explicitly permits _.
  - Read (rejected): GET /v1/projects/slug/:slug, param at project-router.ts:383 uses slugSchema().

  slugSchema (in backend/src/server/lib/schemas.ts:14-27) validates via slugify(v, { lowercase: true }) === v. For <text>_<text>, slugify returns <text>-<text> note . the slugify does this (it converts _ → -), which is not equal to the input, so the check fails and the request is rejected before it ever reaches the handler.

 


### To Reproduce

 Steps to reproduce

  1. Create a project (any valid slug, e.g. repro-proj).
  2. Rename it to an underscore slug via update:
  PATCH /api/v1/projects/<projectId>
  { "slug": "repro_test_proj" }
  3. → 200 (update accepts _).
  4. Read it back by that slug:
  GET /api/v1/projects/slug/repro_test_proj
  5. → 400 Slug field can only contain lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.

  Step 4 fails even though step 2 succeeded and the project exists.


### Expected behavior

### Product

Platform/Access controls/Other

### Describe the bug

`error-handler.ts`'s `jwt.JsonWebTokenError` branch maps an expired access token to `403 Forbidden` with message `"Your token has expired. Please re-authenticate."`. The frontend's response interceptor (`config/request.ts`) that's meant to silently refresh on expiry only triggers on `status === 401` plus a substring match for `"token expired"`. Neither matches: wrong status, and the message reads "token **has** expired."

### To Reproduce

1. Log in and stay active until the access token's TTL naturally elapses.
2. Make any API call. It fails with 403, no silent refresh is attempted.
3. Navigate to a protected route: the guard's own token check also fails (see #7822) and bounces to `/login`, despite a still-valid refresh cookie.

### Expected behavior

An expired access token should trigger the existing silent-refresh interceptor and reissue a new token from the still-valid refresh cookie, transparently to the user.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted

### Additional context

Every session eventually gets forcibly logged out once its access token expires, with no recovery, users report intermittent full re-logins. Confirmed by direct comparison of the two literal contracts, `error-handler.ts`'s actual response shape versus `request.ts`'s `isTokenExpiredError()` and `status === 401` guard, and by diffing `error-handler.ts` in full between `master` and the deployed `v0.162.24`, the relevant branch is unchanged. Environment: self-hosted, `v0.162.24`, also present on `master` HEAD.

Proposed fix: either change the interceptor's guard to match on `status === 403 && error === "TokenError"`, or change the backend to return 401 for an expired JWT.

### Product

Platform/Access controls/Other

### Describe the bug

`fetchAuthToken` (`refresh.ts`) uses a bare `axios` import instead of the app's `apiRequest` instance, so it loses the default `Content-Type: application/json` header. The backend only parses JSON, so Fastify's own 415 fires before the route's auth logic runs, and `error-handler.ts` has no branch for Fastify's native error class, masking it as a generic 500.


### To Reproduce

1. Log in, then fully reload the page (or open a protected URL in a new tab) while the session cookie is still valid.
2. The `_authenticate` route guard's own `fetchAuthToken` call hits the masked 500 and treats it as unauthenticated.
3. User is bounced to `/login` with an "Access Restricted" toast, despite having a valid session.

### Expected behavior

A valid session cookie should survive a page reload. A content-type mismatch on `/api/v1/auth/token` should surface as 415, not an opaque 500 that the route guard can't distinguish from "not logged in".

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted

### Additional context

### Actual Behavior

Every reload/new-tab/deep-link into a protected route while `fetchAuthToken`'s in-memory token is empty forces this call, and it always fails, kicking an authenticated user back to `/login`.

### Environment

- Self-hosted, `v0.162.24`, also present on `master` HEAD

### Additional Information

Verified with a `curl` reproduction, the matching server-side stack trace by request ID, and a full trace of `root.tsx`/`authenticate.tsx`/`refresh.ts`/`request.ts`, confirmed identical between `master` and `v0.162.24`.

### Proposed solution

In `refresh.ts`, use `apiRequest` instead of the bare `axios` import so the call gets the app's default JSON header. Separately, add a branch in the error handler for Fastify's native `FastifyError` so any future content-type mismatch surfaces its real status instead of a masked 500.

### Product

Secret Manager

### Describe the bug

When using a self-hosted Infisical deployment secured by a private/internal CA hierarchy, the operator successfully validates connectivity and authentication but fails to reconcile `InfisicalStaticSecret` resources with a TLS trust error.

The configured `InfisicalConnection` references a CA bundle via:

```yaml
spec:
  tls:
    caCertificate:
      name: infisical-ca
      namespace: <namespace>
      key: ca.crt
```

The connection becomes healthy:

```text
InfisicalConnection   Ready=True
```

and authentication succeeds:

```text
InfisicalAuth         Ready=True
```

Operator logs show successful Kubernetes authentication and credential caching:

```text
successful authentication with "kubernetes"
Reusing cached authentication
```

However, `InfisicalStaticSecret` reconciliation fails:

```text
InfisicalStaticSecret Synced=False
```

with the following error:

```text
failed to fetch secrets:
unable to fetch all secret sources:
failed to list secrets:

tls: failed to verify certificate:
x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

## Why This Appears Unexpected

The CA bundle configured in the `InfisicalConnection` has been independently validated.

Using the exact CA bundle stored in the Kubernetes Secret:

```bash
curl --cacert ca.pem https://<infisical-host>/api/status
```

returns:

```text
SSL certificate verify ok
HTTP/2 200
```

and the exact API endpoint used by the operator also validates successfully:

```bash
curl --cacert ca.pem \
  "https://<infisical-host>/api/v4/secrets?..."
```

returns:

```text
SSL certificate verify ok
HTTP/2 401 Unauthorized
```

The `401 Unauthorized` response is expected because no authentication token was supplied. The important observation is that TLS verification succeeds successfully using the same CA bundle referenced by `InfisicalConnection`.

## Expected Behaviour

The CA certificate configured on the `InfisicalConnection` should be used

### To Reproduce

1. Deploy a self-hosted Infisical instance using a certificate issued by a private/internal certificate authority.

2. Create a Kubernetes Secret that contains the CA certificate chain used to validate the Infisical endpoint.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: infisical-ca
  namespace: <namespace>
type: Opaque
stringData:
  ca.crt: |
    -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
    ...
    -----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

3. Create an `InfisicalConnection` referencing the CA certificate.

```yaml
apiVersion: secrets.infisical.com/v1beta1
kind: InfisicalConnection
metadata:
  name: self-hosted-infisical
spec:
  address: https://<infisical-host>

  tls:
    caCertificate:
      name: infisical-ca
      namespace: <namespace>
      key: ca.crt
```

4. Verify that the connection becomes healthy.

```bash
kubectl get infisicalconnection
```

Expected:

```text
READY=True
```

5. Create an `InfisicalAuth` using Kubernetes authentication.

```yaml
apiVersion: secrets.infisical.com/v1beta1
kind: InfisicalAuth
...
```

6. Verify that authentication becomes healthy.

```bash
kubectl get infisicalauth
```

Expected:

```text
READY=True
```

7. Create an `InfisicalStaticSecret` referencing the authentication resource.

```yaml
apiVersion: secrets.infisical.com/v1beta1
kind: InfisicalStaticSecret
...
```

8. Observe the `InfisicalStaticSecret` status and operator logs.

```bash
kubectl describe infisicalstaticsecret <name>
kubectl logs -n infisical-operator deployment/<operator-deployment>
```

## Actual Result

`InfisicalStaticSecret` reconciliation fails with:

```text
failed to fetch secrets:
unable to fetch all secret sources:
failed to list secrets:

tls: failed to verify certificate:
x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

## Additional Validation

The same CA bundle referenced by the `InfisicalConnection` successfully validates the Infisical endpoint:

```bash
curl --cacert ca.pem https://<infisical-host>/api/status
```

Result:

```text
SSL certificate verify ok
HTTP/2 200
```

The same CA bundle also successfully validates the exact secrets API endpoint used by the operator:

```bash
curl --cacert ca.pem \
  "https://<infisical-host>/api/v4/secrets?environment=<env>&projectId=<id>&recursive=false&secretPath=<path>"
```

Result:

```text
SSL certificate verify ok
HTTP/2 401 Unauthorized
```

The `401 Unauthorized` response is expected 

### Expected behavior

When an `InfisicalConnection` is configured with a valid CA bundle using:

```yaml
spec:
  tls:
    caCertificate:
      name: infisical-ca
      namespace: <namespace>
      key: ca.crt
```

all operator communication with the Infisical API should use that CA bundle consistently.

If `InfisicalConnection` reports:

```text
Ready=True
```

and `InfisicalAuth` reports:

```text
Ready=True
```

then `InfisicalStaticSecret` reconciliation should be able to establish a trusted TLS connection to the Infisical API using the same CA bundle.

For private PKI deployments, the following workflow should succeed:

```text
InfisicalConnection   Ready=True
InfisicalAuth         Ready=True
InfisicalStaticSecret Synced=True
```

and the target Kubernetes Secret should be created or updated successfully.

A CA bundle that successfully validates:

- `/api/status`
- `/api/v4/secrets`

outside of the operator should also be sufficient for secret synchronization within the operator.

The operator should not return:

```text
x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

when the configured CA bundle is capable of successfully validating the certificate chain presented by the Infisical endpoint.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted

### Additional context

_No response_

### Product

Secret Manager

### Describe the bug

`docs/cli/commands/service-token.mdx` tells the reader the command can do three things:

> The Infisical `service-token` command allows you to manage service tokens for a given Infisical project. With this command, you can **create, view, and delete** service tokens.

Only `create` exists. The same page then documents nothing but a `service-token create` accordion, so the page contradicts itself two paragraphs apart.

The CLI agrees with the accordion, not the sentence:

```
$ infisical service-token --help
Manage service tokens

Usage:
  infisical service-token
  infisical service-token [command]

Examples:
infisical service-token

Available Commands:
  create      Used to create service tokens

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for service-token
```

`packages/cmd/tokens.go` in `Infisical/cli` registers exactly one subcommand, and defines no others:

```go
tokensCmd.AddCommand(tokensCreateCmd)

RootCmd.AddCommand(tokensCmd)
```

There is no `tokensViewCmd` and no `tokensDeleteCmd` anywhere in the file.

The practical cost is small but real: someone who has issued a token from the CLI and wants to revoke it goes looking for `infisical service-token delete` and has to work out on their own that revocation only exists in the web UI and the API. Bare `infisical service-token` does not help either — it requires a login and then returns, because `tokensCmd`'s `Run` body is empty — so nothing lists tokens anywhere in the CLI, which makes "view" look like it ought to be a subcommand that simply went missing.

### To Reproduce

1. Install the CLI and run:

```
$ infisical service-token --help      # create is the only subcommand

$ infisical service-token view
Error: accepts 0 arg(s), received 1
Usage:
  infisical service-token
  infisical service-token [command]

$ infisical service-token delete
Error: accepts 0 arg(s), received 1
Usage:
  infisical service-token
  infisical service-token [command]
```

2. Neither word is a subcommand, so cobra reads it as a positional argument and rejects it against `Args: cobra.ExactArgs(0)`.

3. Compare against https://infisical.com/docs/cli/commands/service-token, which says the command can "create, view, and delete" service tokens.

### Expected behavior

Correct the description to match the command — it creates service tokens — and, if it is useful, point readers at where a token can actually be viewed and revoked. Adding `view` and `delete` subcommands would work too, but the one-line doc fix is what makes the page stop contradicting itself.

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted

### Additional context

CLI `infisical version 0.41.90`, macOS. Docs read from the repository at `ba678da03bfa40ddee2608ada24b6edd8c7817a1`; the code quoted above is from the current `Infisical/cli` `packages/cmd/tokens.go`, where it still holds.

This is only about the create/view/delete sentence. The deprecation warning that used to head the same page is separate and already handled by #7740.

### Product

Platform/Access controls/Other

### Describe the bug

`docs/cli/commands/commands.mdx` is the CLI's overview page, and both of its tables are stale.

**The command table lists four commands.** The CLI ships far more:

```
| Command | Description                                                          |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `login` | Used to authenticate and set the logged in user.                     |
| `init`  | Used to link a local project to the platform.                        |
| `run`   | Used to inject envars from the platform into an application process. |
| `vault` | Used to manage where your login credentials are stored at rest       |
```

`docs/cli/commands/` itself has 22 command pages — `secrets`, `export`, `token`, `user`, `reset`, `service-token`, `scan`, `gateway`, `kmip`, `pam`, `relay`, `dynamic-secrets`, `bootstrap`, `agent-proxy` and more — so this page contradicts its own sibling pages in the same directory, and the sidebar shows commands the overview says do not exist.

**The global options table lists `--debug`, `-d`, which does not exist.**

```
| Option            | Description                                     |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `--help`, `-h`    | List help for any command                       |
| `--debug`, `-d`   | Enable verbose logging                          |
| `--domain`        | Use to direct Infisical to a self-hosted domain |
| `--version`, `-v` | Print version information and quit              |
```

There is no `--debug` flag and no `-d` shorthand on the root command. Verbose logging is `--log-level` / `-l`. The table also omits `--silent` and `--telemetry`, which do exist.

`packages/cmd/root.go` in `Infisical/cli` registers exactly these persistent flags:

```go
RootCmd.PersistentFlags().StringP("log-level", "l", "", "log level (trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal)")
RootCmd.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&logFormat, "log-format", "", ...)
RootCmd.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&logDestination, "log-destination", "", ...)
RootCmd.PersistentFlags().Bool("telemetry", true, ...)
RootCmd.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&config.INFISICAL_URL, "domain", ..., ...)
RootCmd.PersistentFlags().Bool("silent", false, ...)
```

No `debug`. The word "debug" appears on that page only inside `--log-level`'s own value list, which is likely where the confusion started.

Someone following this page will try `infisical --debug`, get `unknown flag: --debug`, and will not find `secrets`, `export` or `service-token` documented as existing commands at all.

### To Reproduce

1. Install the CLI and run `infisical --help`:

```
Available Commands:
  agent           Used to launch a client daemon that streamlines authentication and secret retrieval processes in various environments
  bootstrap       Used to bootstrap your Infisical instance
  dynamic-secrets Used to list dynamic secrets
  export          Used to export environment variables to a file
  gateway         Run the Infisical gateway or manage its systemd service
  help            Help about any command
  init            Used to connect your local project with Infisical project
  kmip            Used to manage KMIP servers
  login           Login into your Infisical account
  reset           Used to delete all Infisical related data on your machine
  run             Used to inject environments variables into your application process
  scan            Scan for leaked secrets in git history, directories, and files
  secrets         Used to create, read update and delete secrets
  service-token   Manage service tokens
  ssh             Used to issue SSH credentials
  token           Manage your access tokens
  user            Used to manage local user credentials
  vault           Used to manage where your Infisical login token is saved on your machine

Flags:
      --domain string      Point the CLI to your own backend [can also set via environment variable name: INFISICAL_API_URL] (default "https://app.infisical.com/api")
  -h, --help               help for infisical
  -l, --log-level string   log level (trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal) (default "info")
      --silent             Disable output of tip/info messages. Useful when running in scripts or CI/CD pipelines.
      --telemetry          Infisical collects non-sensitive telemetry data to enhance features and improve user experience. Participation is voluntary (default true)
  -v, --version            version for infisical
```

2. Compare against https://infisical.com/docs/cli/commands/commands — four commands, and a `--debug` that is not in the Flags block above.

3. `infisical --debug` returns `unknown flag: --debug`.

### Product

Secret Manager

### Describe the bug

`infisical secrets delete <NAME>` always fails with HTTP 404 "Secret not found" for ordinary (shared) secrets, even ones created seconds earlier with `infisical secrets set`.

Cause: the delete command's `--type` flag defaults to `personal`, while `secrets set` defaults to `shared`. The backend then looks up a personal secret with that name, finds none, and returns 404 (`DELETE /api/v3/secrets/raw/<NAME>`). Passing `--type shared` explicitly makes the same delete succeed.

The mismatch is visible in `packages/cmd/secrets.go`: `secretsSetCmd` registers `--type` with default `util.SECRET_TYPE_SHARED`, `secretsDeleteCmd` registers it with default `"personal"`.

The error message ("Please make sure your secret path, workspace and environment name are all correct.") gives no hint that the secret type is the mismatched parameter.

### To Reproduce

1. Log in (`infisical login`, user auth) and connect a project (`infisical init`).
2. `infisical secrets set TEST_DELETE_ME=x --env dev`
3. `infisical secrets get TEST_DELETE_ME --env dev` — succeeds, shows type `shared`.
4. `infisical secrets delete TEST_DELETE_ME --env dev` — fails: `Response Code: 404 Not Found`, `Message: Secret not found` (e.g. request ID `req-eu-L2DaXAovylHn9p`).
5. `infisical secrets delete TEST_DELETE_ME --env dev --type shared` — succeeds.

Also reproduced with: `--path /`, explicit `--projectId`, plural name args, and running outside any `.infisical.json` directory — all 404 without `--type shared`.

### Expected behavior

Deleting a secret created by `infisical secrets set` should work without extra flags — the two commands should agree on the default secret type (or the delete should fall back to the shared secret when no personal one exists, or the error should name the type mismatch).

### Screenshots

N/A

### Deployment Type

Infisical Cloud

### Additional context

(Deployment is EU, https://eu.infisical.com)

- CLI v0.43.125 and v0.41.99 (linux amd64, GitHub release binaries) both reproduce identically — present at least since the CLI moved to the dedicated repo (commit `9c3717a4`), inherited from the monorepo.
- OS: Linux (WSL2, Ubuntu). Auth: interactive user login, file vault.
- `secrets set` (create and update), `secrets get`, `secrets` (list), `export`, `run`, and `secrets folders create/delete` all work against the same project/environment; only `secrets delete` is affected.
- Free tier, single project, default `/` path, no folders or approval policies involved.
- Docs mismatch: the CLI docs for `secrets set` state `--type` "defaults to shared", while the `secrets delete` docs do not document a `--type` flag at all — the `personal` default on delete is undocumented (https://infisical.com/docs/cli/commands/secrets).

### Product

Platform/Machine identities

### Describe the bug

The update flows for 8 identity auth methods share a copy-pasted TTL validation:

```ts
if (
  (accessTokenMaxTTL || identityGcpAuth.accessTokenMaxTTL) > 0 &&
  (accessTokenTTL || identityGcpAuth.accessTokenMaxTTL) > (accessTokenMaxTTL || identityGcpAuth.accessTokenMaxTTL)
) {
  throw new BadRequestError({ message: "Access token TTL cannot be greater than max TTL" });
}
```

On the left side of the comparison, when `accessTokenTTL` is omitted from the request, the fallback is the stored `accessTokenMaxTTL`. It should be the stored `accessTokenTTL` — the check is supposed to compare the effective TTL against the effective max TTL.

The result: **lowering only `accessTokenMaxTTL` is rejected even when the stored TTL is well below the new max.**

Affected update flows (left-side fallback is `accessTokenMaxTTL`):

- `identity-gcp-auth-service.ts` (`updateGcpAuth`)
- `identity-kubernetes-auth-service.ts` (`updateKubernetesAuth`)
- `identity-oidc-auth-service.ts` (`updateOidcAuth`)
- `identity-jwt-auth-service.ts` (`updateJwtAuth`)
- `identity-azure-auth-service.ts` (`updateAzureAuth`)
- `identity-aws-auth-service.ts` (`updateAwsAuth`)
- `identity-token-auth-service.ts` (`updateTokenAuth`)
- `identity-ua-service.ts` (`updateUniversalAuth`)

The five newer auth methods already do this correctly with `accessTokenTTL` as the left-side fallback: `identity-alicloud-auth`, `identity-ldap-auth`, `identity-oci-auth`, `identity-spiffe-auth`, `identity-tls-cert-auth`. The differential between the two groups is what makes the intended semantics unambiguous.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a machine identity with Universal Auth: `accessTokenTTL = 3600` (1h), `accessTokenMaxTTL = 2592000` (30d).
2. `PATCH /api/v1/auth/universal-auth/identities/:identityId` with body `{ "accessTokenMaxTTL": 604800 }` (7d), without re-sending `accessTokenTTL`.
3. Response is `400 Access token TTL cannot be greater than max TTL`, because the check compares the stored **max** TTL (30d) against the new max (7d) instead of the stored TTL (1h).

### Expected behavior

The update succeeds: the effective TTL after the update (1h, unchanged) is below the new max TTL (7d). Re-sending `accessTokenTTL: 3600` alongside the max-TTL change makes the same request pass, which shows the stored-TTL comparison is what was intended.

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted

### Additional context

Minor related cleanup: `identity-azure-auth-service.ts` names the row variable `identityGcpAuth` (copy-paste from the GCP service).

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

### Product

Platform/Access controls/Other

### Describe the bug

A Machine Identity with **JWT Auth** and an **Audiences** bound claim returns a
500 when the presented token's `aud` is a JSON array rather than a scalar string —
even when the configured audience is a member of that array:

```
POST /api/v1/auth/jwt-auth/login
HTTP 500  { "statusCode": 500, "error": "Internal Server Error", "message": "Something went wrong" }
```

Removing the Audiences constraint lets the same token authenticate (`200`), which
isolates the failure to the audience comparison. Array-valued `aud` is spec-legal
(RFC 7519 §4.1.3) and is the guaranteed shape of every Kubernetes ServiceAccount
token, so this blocks any Kubernetes workload using JWT Auth.



### To Reproduce

1. Create a Machine Identity with **JWT Auth** / **JWKS**, setting **Audiences** to
   `infisical` and Subject to `system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa>`.
2. Mint a token whose `aud` array contains that audience:
   ```
   kubectl create token <sa> -n <ns> --audience infisical --duration 1h
   ```
   → payload contains `"aud": ["infisical"]`.
3. Attempt login:
   ```
   curl -sS -X POST https://eu.infisical.com/api/v1/auth/jwt-auth/login \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"identityId":"<id>","jwt":"<token>"}'
   ```
   → **`HTTP 500 "Something went wrong"`**.

Removing the Audiences constraint and retrying the same token → **`200`**.

### Expected behavior

The audience check should treat `aud` as a set: accept when the configured audience
is a member, return `401` when it isn't. It should never throw a `500` on a
spec-legal claim shape, regardless of comparison semantics.


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Deployment Type

Infisical Cloud

### Additional context

#### Environment

- Infisical Cloud, EU region (`eu.infisical.com`), observed 2026-07-28
- Machine Identity → JWT Auth, JWKS configuration
- Token issuer: Kubernetes ServiceAccount OIDC issuer (RS256), JWKS served publicly
- Reproduced server-side with `curl`; originally hit via External Secrets Operator

#### Specification references

- **RFC 7519 §4.1.3** — `aud` is an array of case-sensitive strings, with a single
  string permitted as shorthand for the one-audience case; the array is the general
  form. https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.3
- **Kubernetes TokenRequest** — `spec.audiences` is a list, so issued tokens always
  serialize `aud` as an array.
  https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/authentication-resources/token-request-v1/

#### Request ID

- `req-i5q6h5ZJs2EcXP`

#### Workaround

Drop the Audiences constraint and rely on Issuer + Subject bound claims (loses
audience scoping).

### Product

Secrets Management

### Describe the bug

In the Go sidecar (`backend-go`), a **relative** secret reference that appears inside a secret reached through an **absolute** reference is resolved against the *requesting* board's environment/path instead of the referenced secret's own environment/path.

Given `dev` and `prod` that both define `HOST`:

| env | key | value |
|---|---|---|
| dev | `HOST` | `dev-host` |
| dev | `API_URL` | `${prod.URL}` |
| prod | `HOST` | `prod-host` |
| prod | `URL` | `https://${HOST}/api` |

Reading `API_URL` from `dev` returns:

- Node (`/api/v4/secrets`): `https://prod-host/api`
- Go sidecar: `https://dev-host/api`

The Go expander never even issues a read for `prod:/:HOST` — it resolves `${HOST}` from its `localLookup` map, which only ever contains secrets from the requested board (plus its imports).

### Root cause

`SecretExpander.expandValue` carries no notion of which environment/path the value it is expanding belongs to:

https://github.com/Infisical/infisical/blob/main/backend-go/internal/services/secretmanager/secret/expansion.go#L203-L218

```go
if len(parts) == 1 {
    // Relative reference: ${KEY}
    found = true // Always replace relative refs (with empty if not found)
    if sec := e.localLookup[parts[0]]; sec != nil {
```

`localLookup` is built once in `NewSecretExpander` from the secrets of the requested board. When the expander recurses into a secret fetched via `FetchAbsoluteSecrets` (a different env/path), single-part references inside that value still hit `localLookup`.

Node does the opposite — it pushes the *referenced* secret's own `environment` / `secretPath` onto the expansion stack, so subsequent single-part refs resolve there:

https://github.com/Infisical/infisical/blob/main/backend/src/services/secret-v2-bridge/secret-reference-fns.ts#L427-L459

```ts
const node = {
  value: referencedSecretValue,
  secretPath: referencedSecretPath,
  environment: referencedSecretEnvironmentSlug,
  ...
};
...
stack.push({ ...node, visitedSecrets: newVisitedSecrets });
```

and the relative branch then reads from that popped context:

```ts
if (entities.length === 1) {
  const [secretKey] = entities;
  const referredValue = await fetchSecret(environment, secretPath, secretKey);
```

### Impact

Both backends serve `/api/v4/secrets`, and the Go sidecar is shadow-compared against Node in `backend/src/server/plugins/go-sidecar-shadowing.ts`, so this shows up as a `value_mismatch`.

Beyond the mismatch, the resolved value is wrong in a way that crosses an environment boundary: the value returned for a `prod` reference is composed from `dev` data. Anyone who can write a secret in `dev` can change what a `${prod....}` reference expands to, as long as the prod secret contains a relative reference. The permission callback (`CanAccessAbsolute`) is not bypassed — prod's own value is still access-checked — but the substituted content silently comes from the lower environment.

It also fails closed in the opposite direction: if the key does not exist on the requesting board, the reference expands to empty rather than reading the correct value from the referenced environment.

### To Reproduce

Add to `backend-go/internal/services/secretmanager/secret/expansion_test.go`:

```go
func TestExpand_NestedRelativeUsesReferencedEnv(t *testing.T) {
	secrets := []*ProcessedSecret{
		newTestSecret("HOST", "dev-host", "dev", "/"),
		newTestSecret("API_URL", "${prod.URL}", "dev", "/"),
	}

	var requested []string
	opts := ExpandOpts{
		FetchAbsoluteSecrets: func(refs []AbsoluteSecretRef) []*ProcessedSecret {
			var out []*ProcessedSecret
			for _, ref := range refs {
				requested = append(requested, ref.CacheKey())
				switch {
				case ref.Env == "prod" && ref.Key == "URL":
					out = append(out, newTestSecret("URL", "https://${HOST}/api", "prod", "/"))
				case ref.Env == "prod" && ref.Key == "HOST":
					out = append(out, newTestSecret("HOST", "prod-host", "prod", "/"))
				}
			}
			return out
		},
	}

	NewSecretExpander(secrets, opts).Expand()

	t.Logf("refs requested: %v", requested)
	assert.Equal(t, "https://prod-host/api", secrets[1].Value)
}
```

Result on `main`:

```
expansion_test.go: refs requested: [prod:/:URL]
    Error:      Not equal:
                expected: "https://prod-host/api"
                actual  : "https://dev-host/api"
```

Note `prod:/:HOST` is never requested.

### Expected behavior

A relative reference inside a secret reached through an absolute reference resolves against that secret's own environment and path, matching Node. In the example above, `dev`'s `API_URL` expands to `https://prod-host/api`.

### Additional context

The existing test `TestExpand_AbsoluteReference_WithNestedRelative` currently asserts the divergent behavior, which is why this has not surfaced — its `FetchAbsoluteSecrets` mock returns the same secret regardless of which refs are requested, so the prod-side key is never exercised.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR shortly.

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted / Cloud (backend-go sidecar)

## Describe the bug

`GET /api/status` writes two `logger.info` lines on **every** request — a summary line and a full `JSON.stringify(histogram, null, 2)` dump of the event-loop delay histogram:

https://github.com/Infisical/infisical/blob/main/backend/src/server/routes/index.ts

```ts
handler: async () => {
  const cfg = getConfig();
  const serverCfg = await getServerCfg();

  const meanLagMs = histogram.mean / 1e6;
  const maxLagMs = histogram.max / 1e6;
  const p99LagMs = histogram.percentile(99) / 1e6;

  logger.info(`Event loop stats - Mean: ...`);
  logger.info(`Raw event loop stats: ${JSON.stringify(histogram, null, 2)}`);
  ...
```

`/api/status` is the natural health endpoint, so in any orchestrated deployment it is called by a liveness/readiness probe on a fixed interval. In our Kubernetes deployment (the official `infisical-standalone` Helm chart) the readiness probe is `GET /api/status` with `period=5s`, which turns this into a continuous log stream.

Introduced in #3282 (merged 2025-03-20), still present in `v0.162.12`.

## Impact

Measured on a single-replica self-hosted instance, `infisical/infisical:v0.162.10`, one hour of container logs:

| | |
|---|---|
| `/api/status` requests | 720/h (readiness probe, every 5s) |
| Log records produced by them | 1440/h — ~34,500/day |
| Bytes of the `Raw event loop stats` dump alone | 826 KB/h |
| Total log bytes for the container | 1.81 MB/h |
| **Share of the container's log volume** | **~45%** |

That is ~20 MB/day, ~0.6 GB/month of log ingest per replica for a single message. On a hosted log backend this is a real line item, and it buries the lines that actually matter — the same hour contained only 347 `getPlan` lines and 173 `injectPermission` lines.

There is no way to turn it off: the calls are unconditional, not gated by `LOG_LEVEL` or any env var.

## The logged values are also not usable as-is

The histogram is created once at startup and never `.reset()`, so every field is cumulative over the process lifetime:

```json
{
  "count": 8000542,
  "min": 376832,
  "max": 5553258495,
  "mean": 20116550.6745398,
  "percentiles": { "50": 20103168, "99.99998807907104": 5549064192 }
}
```

- `count: 8000542` × 20 ms resolution ≈ 44.4 h — exactly the pod's age. Nothing is ever windowed.
- `mean` (20.1 ms) and `p50`/`p75` sit on the sampling-resolution floor, i.e. the loop is idle. They will read ~20 ms forever regardless of load.
- `max: 5.55 s` is one stall that happened at some unknown point in the last 44 hours. It is frozen in `max` and in the top percentiles for the rest of the process's life and cannot decay.

So the numbers cannot show a trend, cannot be alerted on, and become less informative the longer the process runs — while costing half the log volume.

## Suggested fix

Any of these would resolve it; (1) is the smallest:

1. Demote both lines to `logger.debug`. One-line change, keeps the diagnostic available for anyone who raises `LOG_LEVEL`.
2. Remove them. The same data is already exported properly when telemetry is enabled: `initTelemetryInstrumentation` registers `RuntimeNodeInstrumentation`, which emits `nodejs.eventloop.delay.{min,max,mean,stddev,p50,p90,p99}` as real time-series via the Prometheus/OTLP exporter — windowed, alertable, and not tied to how often a probe hits the health endpoint.
3. If the logging is worth keeping, move it out of the request handler onto a fixed timer and `histogram.reset()` after each emit, so the values describe the last interval rather than the whole process lifetime.

Happy to open a PR for (1) if that is the direction you'd prefer.

## Environment

- Infisical `v0.162.10` (verified the code is unchanged in `v0.162.12`)
- Self-hosted, `infisical-standalone` Helm chart 1.10.0, Kubernetes

### Describe the bug

The infisical-standalone Helm chart always renders literal DB_CONNECTION_URI and REDIS_URL environment variables when postgresql.enabled=true and redis.enabled=true.

This makes it difficult or impossible to configure the Infisical application container using Kubernetes Secrets only. Even when infisical.kubeSecretRef points to a Secret containing DB_CONNECTION_URI and REDIS_URL, the explicitly rendered env entries override the envFrom values.

The chart also supports existing Secrets for the Bitnami PostgreSQL/Redis subcharts, but those Secret values are not used when generating the Infisical application’s own DB_CONNECTION_URI and REDIS_URL.



### To Reproduce

1. Install or render infisical-standalone with bundled PostgreSQL and Redis enabled:
infisical:
  kubeSecretRef: infisical-secrets

postgresql:
  enabled: true
  auth:
    username: infisical
    existingSecret: infisical-postgresql
    database: infisicalDB

redis:
  enabled: true
  auth:
    existingSecret: infisical-redis

2. Create infisical-secrets containing:
DB_CONNECTION_URI: postgresql://infisical:<password>@postgresql:5432/infisicalDB
REDIS_URL: redis://:<password>@redis-master:6379

3. Render the chart:
helm template infisical infisical-helm-charts/infisical-standalone \
  --namespace infisical \
  --values values.yaml

4. Inspect the rendered Infisical Deployment.

5. Observe that the container has explicit env vars:
- name: DB_CONNECTION_URI
  value: postgresql://...
- name: REDIS_URL
  value: redis://...

These values are generated from Helm values, not from the referenced Kubernetes Secret.

### Expected behavior

The chart should allow DB_CONNECTION_URI and REDIS_URL for the Infisical application container to come from Kubernetes Secrets without requiring plaintext passwords in Helm values.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted

### Additional context

Chart tested:
infisical-helm-charts/infisical-standalone

chart version: 1.9.0
app version: 1.0.1

This matters because storing passwords directly in Helm values can leak secrets into Git, Helm release history, CI logs, etc.

I can open a PR for this if the direction makes sense.

My suggested fix would be:

- Change the PostgreSQL env rendering from two independent `if` blocks to `if` / `else if`, so `DB_CONNECTION_URI` is not rendered twice when `postgresql.useExistingPostgresSecret.enabled=true`.

- Add equivalent SecretRef support for Redis, for example `redis.useExistingRedisSecret`, so `REDIS_URL` can also come from a Kubernetes Secret instead of requiring the Redis password in Helm values.

## Environment
- Self-hosted, Docker Compose deployment (official `infisical/infisical` image)
- Reproduced on both `v0.161.5` and `v0.161.10`
- Reverse proxy: Traefik -> Cloudflare in front (headers pass through cleanly, confirmed via manual curl reproduction)

## Bug
Several endpoints that are called with an intentionally empty body (no `Content-Type` header, `Content-Length: 0` — correct behavior per the client, since there's nothing to send) fail server-side with:

```
FastifyError: Unsupported Media Type
    at ContentTypeParser.run (/backend/node_modules/fastify/lib/content-type-parser.js:195:16)
    at Object.handleRequest (/backend/node_modules/fastify/lib/handle-request.js:50:48)
    at runPreParsing (/backend/node_modules/fastify/lib/route.js:651:19)
    at next (/backend/node_modules/fastify/lib/hooks.js:236:9)
    at handleResolve (/backend/node_modules/fastify/lib/hooks.js:253:7)
code: 'FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE', statusCode: 415
```

The response returned to the client is a 500 (`{"statusCode":500,"message":"Something went wrong","error":"InternalServerError"}`) rather than the underlying 415.

### Endpoints observed affected
- `POST /api/v1/user/me/webauthn/register` — **consistently reproduces, 100% of attempts**, on both versions tested. This makes it impossible to register a new WebAuthn/passkey credential on affected instances.
- `POST /api/v1/auth/token` — intermittent, observed during MFA code submission (some attempts fail, retry sometimes succeeds).
- `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` — intermittent, same signature.

Confirmed via browser DevTools Network tab that the actual request sent has no `Content-Type` header at all and `Content-Length: 0` — this is valid per the Fetch/HTTP spec for a bodyless POST. Manually replaying requests with an explicit `Content-Type: application/json` header (even with an empty `{}` body) does not reproduce the error, which points at Fastify's content-type parser not gracefully handling the "no body, no Content-Type header" case on these particular routes/hooks.

### Steps to reproduce (most reliable: WebAuthn registration)
1. Log in to a self-hosted instance.
2. Go to Personal Settings -> Authentication -> add a new Passkey/WebAuthn device.
3. Click "Add".

**Expected:** Server returns WebAuthn registration challenge options.
**Actual:** 500 Internal Server Error every time; backend log shows `FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_MEDIA_TYPE` as above.

## Impact
Blocks adding/re-adding WebAuthn passkeys entirely on affected self-hosted instances. Also causes occasional login/logout failures requiring a retry.

Happy to provide more logs/details if useful.

### Product

Certificate Manager (PKI)

### Describe the bug


When renewing a certificate via **certificate-v3-service.ts**, the renewal path validates the request against the certificate policy via `certificatePolicyService.validateCertificateRequest`, but the certificateRequest object it builds **(around certificate-v3-service.ts:2417-2434)** never populates basicConstraints from originalCert.isCA. 

The policy's CA-related checks in validateRequestAgainstPolicy **(certificate-policy-service.ts:~307)** are gated on **request.basicConstraints?.isCA === true**, which is always falsy for a renewal request — so a policy that denies CA issuance is silently bypassed on renewal, even though it's correctly enforced on direct issuance (certificate-v3-service.ts:1290, :1608) and on approval (certificate-approval-fns.ts:393).



### To Reproduce

- Create a certificate policy with CA issuance allowed (basicConstraints.isCA: "allowed").
- Issue a CA certificate under that policy.
- Update the policy to deny CA issuance (basicConstraints.isCA: "denied").
- Renew the previously-issued CA certificate.


### Expected behavior

Renewal should be rejected with the same "CA certificate issuance is not allowed by this policy" error that direct issuance and approval paths throw.

### Actual behavior
Renewal succeeds, issuing a new CA-flagged certificate despite the policy now denying it.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Deployment Type

Infisical Cloud also : noting it reproduces on self-hosted too (since the code path is identical) so triage doesn't dismiss it as cloud-only.

### Additional context

The three existing CA-policy checks `(certificate-v3-service.ts:1290, :1608, certificate-approval-fns.ts:393)` are near-identical inline copies rather than calls to one shared function — worth extracting into a single validateCaIssuancePolicy(ca, policy, shouldIssueAsCA) helper in certificate-issuance-utils.ts so the renewal path (and any future issuance path) can't miss it again.

### Product

KMS

### Describe the bug

In backend-go/internal/services/kms/, both ensureProjectDataKey and ensureOrgDataKey open a primary transaction, acquire an advisory lock, and re-check whether a KMS key exists via findProjectKmsInfo(ctx, tx, ...) / findOrgKmsInfo(ctx, tx, ...) — correctly using the transaction handle.
However, in the else branch (key already exists), both functions call decryptInternalKmsKey which hardcodes s.db.Replica().QueryRow() internally and accepts no tx/querier parameter. This means the read escapes the transaction and hits the replica.
Under replication lag, a concurrent request that just created the KMS key on the primary will cause decryptInternalKmsKey to return pgx.ErrNoRows on the replica, producing a Failed to find KMS key error and a 500 for the user.
The inconsistency is visible by comparison — findProjectKmsInfo and findOrgKmsInfo both accept pg.Querier specifically to support both transactional and non-transactional callers. decryptInternalKmsKey was never given the same treatment.

### To Reproduce

## Summary

When the frontend mounts the `/login` route while the browser still holds a
stale `jid` cookie (refresh-token ID that has been rotated or no longer exists
server-side), the React app crashes with
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'component')`
and shows "Something went wrong. Please contact support@infisical.com" instead
of falling through to render the login form. The user is locked out of the UI
until they manually clear cookies for the host or open an incognito window.

The backend behaves correctly — it logs the failure cleanly as an
`AuthTokenNotFound` and returns an error response. The bug is that the frontend
doesn't treat "refresh failed at /login mount" as the normal case it is.

## Environment

- Infisical: `v0.146.0-postgres` (self-hosted, Docker Compose)
- Postgres 16-alpine
- Redis 7-alpine
- Browser: Chrome (latest), accessed over plain HTTP on a LAN
- `SITE_URL` set, `TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false`, no SSO

## Reproduction

1. Sign in to a self-hosted Infisical instance, get the `jid` / refresh-token
   cookie set in the browser.
2. Trigger refresh-token rotation server-side — easiest: sign in on a second
   browser, or restart the Infisical container (rotates state), or wait past
   the refresh-token TTL.
3. Return to the first browser and load `/login`.
4. The `/login` route mounts, fires a refresh attempt against
   `/api/v1/auth/token`, the server returns the `AuthTokenNotFound` error.
5. React crashes; no login form is rendered.

## Expected

`/login` always renders the email/password form. A stale refresh token at mount
should be treated as "no session, show login," not as a fatal error.

## Actual

White error page with "Something went wrong. Please contact
support@infisical.com" and the TypeError above in the browser console.

## Server log signature (correlates with the frontend crash)

```
{"level":50,"severity":"ERROR","err":{
  "type":"NotFoundError",
  "message":"Failed to find refresh token",
  "name":"AuthTokenNotFound",
  "stack":"AuthTokenNotFound: Failed to find refresh token
    at Object.validateRefreshToken (/backend/src/services/auth-token/auth-token-service.ts:157:13)
    at Object.handler (/backend/src/server/routes/v1/auth-router.ts:89:78)
    ..."
}}
```

These come in clusters of 4–33 entries within ~1 second every time the
affected user opens the UI, which suggests the frontend retries the failed
refresh from multiple component mounts.

## Workaround

Clear cookies for the Infisical host (specifically `jid` and any
`infisical_session_*`), then reload. Incognito windows work because they start
with no cookies.

## Suggested fix direction

The `/login` route's auth bootstrap should catch refresh failures (any 4xx
from `/api/v1/auth/token`) and render the login form unconditionally on
failure, rather than letting the error propagate to the React tree.

---

_Bug report drafted with Claude Code (claude.com/code) from self-hosted instance logs and reproduction; filed on behalf of the operator._

### Product

Secret Manager

### Describe the bug

## Summary

`infisical login --method=aws-iam` hits EC2 IMDS at `169.254.169.254` directly
and does not follow the standard AWS SDK credential provider chain. AWS
credentials available via env vars (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` /
`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`), via `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI` (ECS task
role), and even `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true` are all ignored.

This makes `aws-iam` auth effectively unusable on ECS Fargate (no host IMDS
exists), and on EC2-mode ECS it forces the use of the EC2 *instance* role
rather than the *task* role — defeating the per-task identity isolation that
ECS task roles are designed to provide.

## Environment

- CLI: `infisical version 0.43.84` (apt install from official deb repo)
- Container: `python:3.11-slim` (Debian)
- AWS: ECS, both EC2-bridge networking and Fargate
- Region: `us-east-1`

### To Reproduce

Inside an ECS container with a valid task role attached:

```sh
# ECS injects this automatically; container has valid task-role creds via it
echo "$AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI"
# /v2/credentials/abc...

# Fetch task creds and export to env (sanity check that env-var path is set):
CREDS=$(curl -fsS "http://169.254.170.2${AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI}")
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$CREDS" | jq -r .AccessKeyId)
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$CREDS" | jq -r .SecretAccessKey)
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$CREDS" | jq -r .Token)
export AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true

# Verify the env creds work (this succeeds, showing the task role identity):
# aws sts get-caller-identity   # would return task role ARN

infisical login --method=aws-iam --machine-identity-id=$ID --plain
```

### Expected behavior

CLI follows AWS SDK default credential provider chain:
1. Static / env vars (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, etc.)
2. Shared config
3. ECS container creds (`AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI` / `_FULL_URI`)
4. EC2 IMDS

Should auth as the ECS task role.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Deployment Type

Infisical Cloud

### Additional context

_No response_

## Actual

```
error: unable to authenticate with aws iam [err=Put "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)]
```

CLI hits IMDS regardless of env vars and `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true`.

## Impact

ECS users (Fargate especially) cannot use `aws-iam` auth. The only AWS-native
path that *does* work — bumping IMDS hop limit to 2 and using the EC2 instance
role identity — defeats per-task isolation and only applies to EC2-mode tasks.

We're falling back to Universal Auth with the client secret stored in AWS
Secrets Manager. Working but not ideal — `aws-iam` was the right primitive.

## Suggested fix

Use the AWS SDK's default config (`config.LoadDefaultConfig(ctx)`) rather than
a custom IMDS-only credential source for the `aws-iam` login path.
```

### Product

Secret Manager

### Describe the bug

The Bitbucket secret sync (`secret-sync/bitbucket`) silently truncates the existing-variables list to the first page of Bitbucket's API response. When a destination Bitbucket deployment environment has more variables than fit in one page, the sync treats the unseen ones as missing and attempts to `POST /variables/` to create them. Bitbucket then returns `409 Conflict` ("A variable with the key provided already exists for account ..., environment ..."), and the sync fails after partially applying the updates that did fit on page one.

Root cause is in `backend/src/services/secret-sync/bitbucket/bitbucket-sync-fns.ts`, function `listVariables` — unchanged on `main` and confirmed identical in `v0.159.29` (current latest) and `v0.159.28`:

```ts
const url = buildVariablesUrl(workspaceSlug, repositorySlug, environmentId);
const { data } = await request.get<{ values: TBitbucketVariable[] }>(url, { ... });
return data.values;   // ← no pagelen, no next-page follow
```

There is no `pagelen` query parameter and no traversal of the `next` link Bitbucket returns. Bitbucket's default page size for this endpoint is small (around 10), so any env with ~10+ variables hits this every time.

`upsertVariable` decides between `PUT` (update by UUID) and `POST` (create) purely by checking whether the key exists in this in-memory list — so a missing key on page two is misclassified as new, and the POST returns 409.

The same bug affects `deleteVariables` and `syncSecrets`'s `keysToDelete` computation, which can miss variables that exist beyond page one.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a Bitbucket sync targeting a deployment environment.
2. Add 12+ secrets in Infisical at the source path (or have the destination env start with 12+ variables).
3. Run an initial sync — succeeds (POSTs all new variables).
4. Edit any value or trigger another sync.
5. Sync fails. Backend logs show a single `GET /variables/` (response ~1.5 KB containing ~10 entries) followed by one or more `POST /variables/` returning HTTP 409 `ERR_BAD_REQUEST`.

### Expected behavior

`listVariables` should paginate through all pages of Bitbucket's response (e.g. set `?pagelen=100` and follow `data.next` until exhausted) so every existing variable is visible to `upsertVariable` and `deleteVariables`. With the complete list, `PUT` is taken for every matching key and no spurious `POST` is attempted.

### Screenshots / Logs

The error surfaces in the Infisical UI as the verbatim Bitbucket API response forwarded through the sync error handler:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "error": {
      "message": "Conflict",
      "detail": "A variable with the key provided already exists for account {d585026e-7f85-498e-8f0d-179a7cca5864}, environment {ad55b432-047e-42c8-88b2-9fa013802e5c}.",
      "data": {
        "key": "variable-service.variable.duplicate",
        "arguments": {
          "externalId": "{d585026e-7f85-498e-8f0d-179a7cca5864}"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

(Bitbucket error class `variable-service.variable.duplicate` — meaning: "key already exists in the destination env".)

Backend log of the same failing sync (verbose fields trimmed):

```
GET  https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/.../environments/{...}/variables/
  responseSize: 1524
PUT  .../variables/{uuid-1}     200
PUT  .../variables/{uuid-2}     200
... (11 PUTs total)
POST .../variables/             ERR_BAD_REQUEST, status 409
   message: "Request failed with status code 409"
```

After a local fix that adds `?pagelen=100` + a `data.next` loop, the same sync against the same destination:

```
GET  https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/.../environments/{...}/variables/?pagelen=100
  responseSize: 2040
PUT  .../variables/{uuid-1..12}   all 200
"SecretSync Sync Job ... Completed"
```

(no POST, no 409, UI shows "Synced")

### Deployment Type

Self-hosted

### Additional context

- Affects `infisical/infisical:v0.159.29` (current latest) and `v0.159.28` — identical source on both tags
- Bitbucket destination, deployment environment scope
- Workaround until upstream fix: hot-patch `dist/services/secret-sync/bitbucket/bitbucket-sync-fns.mjs` in the running container to append `?pagelen=100` and loop on `data.next` (confirmed working in our environment for the last several hours)
- Happy to open a PR adding pagination to `listVariables` (also covers `deleteVariables` indirectly, since it reuses the same helper)

}

## Summary

`helm-charts/infisical-standalone-postgres/templates/infisical.yaml` renders a fresh timestamp into both the `Deployment` metadata and the pod template on every `helm template` / `helm upgrade`:

```yaml
# lines 7 and 23
updatedAt: {{ now | date "2006-01-01 MST 15:04:05" | quote }}
```

Because this value lands on `spec.template.metadata.annotations`, Kubernetes recomputes the `pod-template-hash` every time the chart re-renders. Under any GitOps controller that reconciles on a schedule — ArgoCD, Flux, Helmfile + cron — this creates a fresh ReplicaSet on every reconcile cycle, continuously rolling pods without any actual change.

## Impact observed (2026-04-17/18, prod)

- `Deployment` revision: **62** in ~17 days on a single-replica prod deployment
- **11 ReplicaSets in 8 hours** on 2026-04-17, each differing only in the `updatedAt` annotation value
- User-visible "Infisical is slow" experience — each rollout leaves a ~30s readiness gap while the new pod bootstraps Node.js (readiness probe also has no configurable `timeoutSeconds`, defaults to 1s — any GC pause > 1s during the window times out the probe)
- `kubectl rollout history` shows revisions with no actual change cause

### Reproduction

```
$ helm template infisical-prod infisical-standalone --version 1.8.0 \
  | grep updatedAt
    updatedAt: "2026-04-17 UTC 23:29:54"
    updatedAt: "2026-04-17 UTC 23:29:54"

$ sleep 7 && helm template infisical-prod infisical-standalone --version 1.8.0 \
  | grep updatedAt
    updatedAt: "2026-04-17 UTC 23:30:01"
    updatedAt: "2026-04-17 UTC 23:30:01"
```

Each render is a different manifest. Any system that applies the second render as an "update" triggers a pod rotation.

## Root cause

`{{ now }}` is non-deterministic. Emitting it into pod-hash-sensitive fields (annotations on `spec.template.metadata`) tells Kubernetes the pod spec changed when the user's intent has not.

## Proposed fix

Remove the `updatedAt` annotation entirely. It provides no operational value (the Deployment's `.status` already tracks `observedGeneration` / `lastTransitionTime`; `kubectl rollout history` tracks revisions). If some consumer truly needs a rendered timestamp, expose it as an opt-in value:

```yaml
{{- if $infisicalValues.emitUpdatedAtAnnotation }}
updatedAt: {{ now | date "2006-01-02 MST 15:04:05" | quote }}
{{- end }}
```

…and document the side effect on the values README.

(Note: the reference format string in the current template uses `2006-01-01` instead of Go's canonical `2006-01-02`. The second `01` happens to collide with the month placeholder so both positions substitute to current month — this is why the observed output has the same two digits in the date portion. Not the cause of the churn, but worth fixing at the same time.)

## Related chart ergonomics

While we're here, these readiness/liveness defaults are aggressive enough to matter in prod:

```yaml
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /api/status
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 5
  # (no timeoutSeconds → K8s defaults to 1s, which is tight for Node.js)
# (no livenessProbe, no startupProbe)
```

Would welcome exposing the probe block as a values knob so operators can tune it without forking the chart:

```yaml
infisical:
  readinessProbe:
    httpGet: {path: /api/status, port: 8080}
    initialDelaySeconds: 10
    periodSeconds: 5
    timeoutSeconds: 5
    failureThreshold: 3
  livenessProbe: { ... }
  startupProbe: { ... }
```

Happy to open the PR myself if this reproduces on your side and you'd accept the fix. Just wanted to file the issue first so other operators can find this thread.

## Environment

- Chart: `infisical-standalone` 1.8.0 (Cloudsmith registry)
- Source: `helm-charts/infisical-standalone-postgres/templates/infisical.yaml` lines 7, 23
- Kubernetes: 1.34.6+rke2r1
- Controller: ArgoCD 3.3.2
- Observed on: production, 2026-04-17 through 2026-04-18

### Describe the bug

PR #5850 fixed an incorrect total count in the project identity membership list endpoint -- the count was summing role assignments instead of unique identities because of a window function running over JOINed `membership_roles` rows.

The same bug exists in two sibling files that weren't covered by that fix:

- `membership-user-dal.ts` (`findUsers`, line ~228)
- `membership-group-dal.ts` (`findGroups`, line ~214)

Both use the same pattern:

```ts
.select(
  db.raw(
    `count(${TableName.Membership}."actorUserId") OVER(PARTITION BY ${TableName.Membership}."scopeOrgId") as total`
  )
)
```

The query JOINs `membership_roles` (one-to-many), so a user with 3 roles produces 3 rows. The window function counts all rows in the partition, returning 8 instead of 5 for an org with 5 users.

`identity-org-dal.ts` (`searchIdentities`, line ~432) has the same issue.

### To reproduce

Given 5 users in an org, where 2 users have multiple roles:

| User | Roles |
|------|-------|
| alice | admin, developer, reviewer |
| bob | member, developer |
| charlie | member |
| diana | member |
| eve | viewer |

**Buggy query result:** `total_count = 8` (3+2+1+1+1)
**Expected result:** `total_count = 5`

Tested on PostgreSQL 14 with the same table structure.

### Expected behavior

Total count should reflect the number of unique users/groups/identities, not the number of role assignments.

### Fix

The same approach from #5850 works here -- replace the window function with a subquery count over the distinct membership set:

```ts
const countQuery = await (tx || db.replicaNode())
  .count("* as total")
  .from(paginatedUsers.clone().as("distinctMemberships"));
```

Happy to open a PR for this if it makes sense to fix all three in one go.

### Describe the bug

There is a race condition in the connection concurrency control used by Secret Sync and PKI Sync.

The counter (`AppConnectionConcurrentJobs`) is managed using separate read and write operations in Redis/keyStore, which are not atomic. Under concurrent load, this can cause the counter to become incorrect and remain permanently elevated.

As a result:
- Sync jobs fail with "concurrency limit reached" even when no jobs are running
- The connection appears permanently busy
- Manual counter reset is required to recover

### To Reproduce

1. Trigger multiple Secret Sync or PKI Sync jobs for the same connection at the same time
2. Observe some jobs failing with "concurrency limit reached"
3. Check Redis – the counter remains > 0 even though no jobs are active
4. Further sync attempts continue to fail

### Expected behavior

The concurrency counter should always reflect the actual number of running jobs. Jobs should only fail when the real limit is reached.

### Root Cause

Current implementation uses a non-atomic pattern:

```ts
const concurrencyCount = await keyStore.getItem(...);
await keyStore.setItemWithExpiry(...);
````

This creates a TOCTOU race condition.

### Suggested Fix

Use the atomic `incrementBy()` method instead:

```ts
await keyStore.incrementBy(key, 1);
await keyStore.incrementBy(key, -1);
```

This should prevent lost updates and stuck counters.

### Impact

* Sync operations can get permanently blocked
* More likely under high load
* Requires manual intervention to fix
items.title: Critical race condition in AppConnectionConcurrentJobs causing sync deadlock

items.body: ### Feature description Improve secret key validation for all import formats (.env, .json, .yml) to prevent users from creating secrets with Unicode or special-character keys. Only allow ASCII-safe keys: A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ - Invalid keys should be rejected or highlighted with a tooltip warning. ### Why would it be useful? Unicode and special characters in secret keys are not supported by most platforms, including: AWS Lambda / ECS / Parameter Store Docker Kubernetes env vars GitHub Actions Vercel / Netlify / Render These keys cannot be mapped into environment variables and often cause deployment failures or missing secrets. Validating them early prevents confusing production issues. ### Additional context - Should prevent users from including JSON or .env files that contain invalid keys in the "Paste Secret Values" modal. - When users enter an invalid key in the "Add secret key" modal, a warning should be displayed to let the user correct it.

### Describe the bug
When applying multiple roles to a machine ID, the final permissions that machine ID will obtain depends on the order in which the roles are applied. 

Moreover, in the "Project Roles" view of a machine identity, the order the roles are display in is alphabetical, rather than the order they were applied in. Thus, there is no way to determine what permissions a machine ID will be granted by looking at the UI. You have to attempt to use the permissions, or re-apply the roles in a known order using the UI.

### To Reproduce
Suppose the goal was to allow any machine with role `allow-both` to Describe Secret and Read Value, but any machine with role `deny-read` may not Read Value. 

1. Go to project > Access Management > Project Roles > Add Role and add `allow-both` role.
2. Click Add Policies > Secrets > Add Policies and select Permission=`Allow`, Actions=[`Describe Secret`, `Read Value`]
3. Click Save on allow-both.
4. Go to project > Access Management > Project Roles > Add Role and add `deny-read` role.
5. Click Add Policies > Secrets > Add Policies and select Permission=`Forbid`, Actions=[`Read Value`]
6. Click Save on `deny-read`.
7. Go to project > Access Management > Machine Identities > Add Identity and select an identity
8. Select Role as `allow-both`, and remove all other roles. Click Add.
9. Click on Edit Role(s) > Add Role and select `deny-read`. Click Save Roles.  
10. Add any secret to the project and attempt to read the value while authenticated as the identity. Permission will be denied. _The `deny-read` role was saved last_.
11. Click Edit Role(s) > and delete `deny-read`. Change the remaining role from `allow-both` to `deny-read` **and click Save Roles**.
12. Click Add Role and select `allow-both`.  Click Save Roles. _The role order is now reversed_
13. Attempt to read the secret value again. Permission will be granted. _The `allow-both` role was saved last_.

Thus, even though both attempts to read the secret had the same roles, the permissions obtained by the machine ID differed. It depends on the order the roles are **saved in**. 

Also note that in the Project Roles view, the roles will appear in alphabetical order (`allow-both` first and `deny-read` second) regardless of the order the roles were added in. This means that someone arriving at the Project Roles page has no way to determine what permissions the MID will obtain just by looking at the roles it has.

### Expected 
It seems that role permissions are applied by summing permissions (with possible inversion) from top to bottom, typically with Forbid coming last. Given that, I would expect that roles follow the same convention, adding permissions top to bottom. 

Additionally, I would expect that the roles can be re-ordered in the Edit Role(s) dialog, to avoid having to shuffle the value as described above. The Project Roles view should then preserve this order rather than an alphabetical ordering.

### Screenshots
N/A

### Platform you are having the issue on:
Running self-hosted in docker x86_64, infisical:v0.146.0-postgres

### Additional context
items.title: Final machine ID permissions depend on the order roles were applied

### Describe the bug
When personal override of some secret is set in one folder `/A`. Secrets from the folder `/A` are imported to another folder `/B`, and than infisical cli is used to export secrets from folder `/B`. In that case the overridden secrets in `/A` are not imported with overridden values, but with the original values. What should happen is that exporting secrets from B, which has imported secrets from A, should in any case contain overridden values of folders A and B.

### To Reproduce
- install infisical CLI
- infisical login with your personal credentials
- create project for secrets called `Proj`
- in `Proj` create folder called `/A`, which contains some secrets
- in `Proj` create folder called `/B`, which has different secrets.
- both folders are on the same level in the `Proj`
- import secrets from `/A` to `/B`
- override single secret with personal override in `/A`
- use Infisical CLI with `export` command to export and save secrets from folder /B to some .env file.
- `infisical export --format=dotenv --projectId=some-guid --env=dev --path=/B --output-file=.env`
- observe that exported secret does not contain overriden values in A
- adding `--secret-overriding=True` flag does not have any effect on the faulty behaviour. 

### Expected behavior
Overridden secrets in A, should be exported with overridden values, not the default ones, when B secrets are exported.

OS: Fedora Linux 42 (Workstation Edition) x86_64
Kernel: Linux 6.17.7-200.fc42.x86_64
